note: 38 AACV notes-side criteria split into nine retrieval groups. Criteria in a group are answered from the same part of the chart, so one search pass serves all of them. WHY: handed all 38 at once the agent searches a handful of topics and then writes every answer without looking anything else up; in two separate ten-patient runs it issued no search at all for the illness group or the DLB group and still answered all twelve of those criteria. Scoping a pass guarantees its group is searched (5.9x more searches per criterion on the one patient measured both ways). WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: the agent still writes every answer after its last retrieval call — 266 of 266 in the grouped passes — so the loop is unchanged, only the criteria-per-search-burst ratio. COST: completing all 38 costs ~69 retrieval calls grouped vs ~12 single-pass (5.8x MORE, not fewer); wall clock was lower on the one patient measured (423s vs 529s) but that is n=1 and token cost is unmeasured. NOT A CONTROLLED COMPARISON: the single-pass and grouped runs used different rubric versions, and an earlier single-pass run on the same patient already decided 2/6 DLB features — the same as the scoped pass — so run-to-run variance matches the claimed effect. Treat this split as reasoned engineering, not as a measured improvement.
